title: Shell-and-tube heat exchanger
goal: A process engineer can trace the separate hot and cold circuits through E-101 and read the outlet temperature-control loop and maintenance connections.

rubric.must: A shell-and-tube exchanger labelled E-101 is the visible centre of the drawing.
Hot glycol and cooling-water process paths are visibly separate circuits through different exchanger connections.
TT-101, TIC-101 and TV-101 form a readable temperature-control loop associated with the hot outlet.
Both circuits show labelled inlet and outlet isolation valves.
A high-point vent and low-point drain are visibly connected to the exchanger.
The temperature-control signal lines are visually distinct from process piping.
Where the hot and cold circuits cross or approach, the picture does not imply they are connected.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the pid exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The diagram clearly labels the central shell-and-tube exchanger E-101. Hot glycol and cooling-water paths use separate exchanger connections; both have labelled inlet and outlet isolation valves. TT-101 is associated with the hot outlet, and the dashed signal path connects it to TIC-101 and TV-101. The vent and drain are visibly connected to the exchanger’s tube-side connections. No ambiguous hot/cold pipe crossing or material overlap is visible.

items.evidence: E-101, labelled “Shell-and-Tube Exchanger,” is prominently centered.

Hot glycol enters the exchanger at the upper left and exits along the lower-right route; cooling water enters on the lower left and returns from the exchanger along the middle-right route. The paths attach to distinct exchanger connections.
TT-101 is shown on the hot outlet line, with a dashed signal to TIC-101 and a distinct dashed command route toward the fail-open TV-101.
XV-101 and XV-102 are labelled on the hot circuit; XV-201 and XV-202 are labelled on the cooling-water circuit.
XV-301 High-point Vent branches from the exchanger’s upper tube-side connection; XV-302 Low-point Drain branches from the lower tube-side connection.
The temperature signal and control routes are dashed, while process piping is shown as solid lines.
The hot and cold process lines remain visually distinct; no crossing suggests a connection between the circuits.
